# 1.2.98 - a GM sets every Remnant's visibility, found or not, on the Investigation dashboard and on the Remnant's own card, a GM sees a player's 3D dice only with that GM's Monokuma in the room, the player's roll window is whole, the table's Hope and Despair dice wear one look, and Set the season up checks the dice look

Stage E60 ships alone with this version (the owner, 01.11.2026: "To zostajemy przy A"). It was planned as "unfound
Remnants only in the GMs' store" (D38 = 2); on 03.11.2026 the owner chose D38 = 1 ("Opcja B wybieram"), so **an unfound
trace stays a hidden token, as at 1.2.97**, and the stage's migration, the GMs' overlay for traces and the token made at
the first find were dropped. What E60 ships: every trace read through one ref, its token with its row of the GMs' store
(C1); the words of D38 = 1 (C2); the visibility band of every Remnant, found or not, on the dashboard's Remnants tab and
on the GM's Remnant card (C4a); D153, a hand-over and the GM's Give in the receiver's finds' queue (C4b); and a dice
group from the owner's feedback after 1.2.97 (C5): Public roll off the GM panel, a light dice look diagnostic in Set the
season up's Pre-season checks, the player's roll window whole, one Hope and Despair look for the table, and a GM's
screen throwing a player's 3D dice only while that GM's Monokuma stands in the roller's room; then a fix round, FG1 to
FG6. **This version adds one world setting, changes who sees a player's 3D dice on a GM's screen and what GMs and players
see; it adds no migration** (Before installing). Nothing in this version has been run at a real table or in Foundry;
what was measured was measured headless, and the gaps are listed in Known gaps and Checked. 20 commits on top of 1.2.97
(main 55f03746, the 1.2.97 release and its local-gate record), up to e8a76c53, the last code commit; no merges.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **A GM who wants to see players' 3D dice switches Dice So Nice's "Show only mine" off** in that GM's own Dice So Nice
   settings (LIVE-E60-09's first step): with it on, a GM's screen draws no other person's dice, whatever the module
   decides. Players should not have it on either, or they miss the dice the module shows them (a Monocub's room, an
   incident); the Dice look part of Pre-season checks names everyone who has it on.
3. **What changes in a running world.**
   - **One new world setting, `diceDualityLook`** (C5d): world scope, not shown in the settings window, `{}` by default,
     of the table's lifetime (the table settings 34 -> 35, R1256), kept by every season reset. It holds the source full
     Gamemaster's Daggerheart Hope, Fear, advantage and disadvantage preset (`{ hope, fear, advantage, disadvantage }`,
     each the preset's names and colours). It is written by the source full Gamemaster's browser alone - at its load, at
     a change of its Daggerheart setting, and when the switch or the source moves to it - only while *One dice look for
     the table* is on and only where Daggerheart keeps such a preset (2.9 and older); the primary GM holds it as it holds
     the dice look switches: a write below full Gamemaster is put back, and a write by any full Gamemaster is held as
     the copy. As every world setting, Foundry sends it to every browser, a player's included, where a console reads it;
     it holds dice names and colours. `world-secrets.mjs` is unchanged: the setting has no row of its own there and is
     read by its rule for every module world setting.
   - No other setting is added, removed or renamed; no client setting is added. Two setting hints are re-worded: *Force
     private player rolls* (the one public roll is a GM's `game.drpg.publicRoll`, a macro) and *One dice look for the
     table* (every Hope and Despair die takes the look that Gamemaster set in Daggerheart, whoever throws it, Daggerheart
     2.9 and older).
   - **The GMs' store `remnants`** (one row per trace; no GM store is added or removed) holds new fields on a trace's
     row: `x`, `y`, `level` (the floor, or null) and `foundAt: null`, written at placement for every trace placed from
     1.2.98 on; `foundAt` and `foundVia` (the road: "find", "reveal", "loot", "gm" ...) at a trace's first find; and
     `gmBand` with `gmBandAt` when a GM sets the trace's band. The spot and the find fields are read by no screen; `gmBand`
     keeps a Reroll off a band a GM set. A row written before 1.2.98 holds none of them and reads as it read.
   - **No migration.** `migrate.mjs` does not change; the migration the stage planned was dropped with D38 = 1. No stored
     data is rewritten and no flag or setting is renamed. An unfound trace is a hidden token from its placement, as at
     1.2.97, and known-leaks S17-64 is held as a Foundry limit the owner accepted (Known gaps); README gains only its
     marker. The language files gain 49 keys in each language and lose 10 in English and 14 in Polish: the GM panel's
     four `DRPG.Panel.publicRoll` keys (`.label`, `.formula`, `.flavour`, `.roll`; `.gmOnly` and `.badFormula` kept) and
     the player window's one-line summary, `DRPG.RollDialog.summary.*` (6 in English, 10 in Polish with `.few` and
     `.many`); three texts change (the two hints and `DRPG.Reroll.traceKept`).
   - **Bridge rows and sockets: no new bridge row, no new socket listener, no new sync kind.** `bridge-wire.mjs` and
     `bridge-table.mjs` do not change; `bridge-guards.mjs` reads a trace through its ref and gains one Reroll reason ("a
     GM set that trace's band"). The dice look diagnostic (C5b, light) asks no other browser anything and sends, posts and
     writes nothing. One existing packet gains a form (FG4): where the primary GM relays a drawn roll's dice, a GM those
     dice do not reach is sent `dice.show { id, subject, quiet: true }` - the roll's character alone - so that GM's card
     is headed with the roller and no die is thrown there.
   - **One new contract row**, `hook-dice-so-nice-roll-start` in `diagnosePatches()`: the module listens to Dice So
     Nice's `diceSoNiceRollStart` on every browser, to lay the table's Hope and Despair look on each throw and keep the
     last throws for the diagnostic. Without it, every Hope and Despair die is drawn in the look its thrower's Daggerheart
     gave it.
   - **For macros and other modules:** `tools/api-surface.json` gains one row, `diagnoseDiceLook`; `publicRoll` stays.
     `game.drpg.remnantsOn` and `game.drpg.remnantsInRoom` now answer frozen refs, not TokenDocuments (C1b): a macro that
     called `.update()` on what they answer breaks (Known gaps). The report of `game.drpg.diagnose()` gains a part, *Dice
     look*, after *Dice*.
   - **What a GM sees differently.**
     - **No Public roll tile** (C5a): the GM panel's "Right now" section loses the tile and its window. The roll stays a
       GM's macro, `game.drpg.publicRoll(formula, { flavor })`, the one roll everybody reads while rolls are forced
       private.
     - **Every Remnant's visibility** (C4a, FG2): the Investigation dashboard's **Remnants** tab has a *Visibility*
       column, a select of the four bands (Obvious, Evident, Subtle, Hidden), for every trace, found or not; it sets the
       Observe roll a finder needs. The Truth Bullets already made keep the band they were made with, and the next
       finder's copy is made at the new one. Double-clicking a Remnant opens its card, where the same select stands in
       place of the band badge and saves on change; both write the row through one road (`setRemnantFlags`). A band change
       marks nothing GM-edited on either road, and a Reroll of the action or the clean-up that left the trace leaves a band
       a GM set (its notice says "a GM has written on it or set its band"). The player's card is unchanged.
     - **A Give from a Remnant** (C4b, D153): Give a Truth Bullet from a Remnant to a student who already holds a copy of
       it gives none and says "{actor} already holds a Truth Bullet of this Remnant, so they get no second one."; the
       check and the bullet run in the receiver's finds' queue with Observe's find, a hand-over and Monokuma's Reveal, on
       one GM's browser (Known gaps).
     - **The Dice look check** (C5b, C5b2, FG3): Set the season up's **Pre-season checks** gain a *Dice look* part - what
       this browser reads of every user's dice look, a cross for each thing that can make the dice look different, a tick
       when there is none - and **Open the dice look**, which opens `game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook()`'s window. On a GM it
       reads every user's Dice So Nice settings and whether each holds the table's look; another person's browser is read
       only on that browser, so each person runs `game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook()` on their own and sends the GM its text.
       `diagnoseDiceLook({ test: true })` throws a Hope and a Fear die on that screen alone; `{ messageId }` reads that
       roll.
     - **A player's 3D dice** (C5e, FG4): with *Force private player rolls* on, a GM's screen throws a player's dice
       only while one of that GM's own Monokumas stands in the roller's room on the same scene; the Monokuma's GM is the
       one whose Despair pool it is. A Monokuma whose GM cannot be told (several full Gamemasters, no pool set and no
       single owner named) admits nobody, and the GM handbook says so. Every GM still reads the card; a GM outside the
       room has it headed with the roller. A GM's own rolls reach every GM's screen, and with *Force private player
       rolls* off every GM sees every roll's dice as before, a Reroll's included.
     - **One Hope and Despair look** (C5d, FG3): with *One dice look for the table* on, every Hope, Fear, advantage and
       disadvantage die on every screen is drawn in the look the source full Gamemaster set in Daggerheart's own Dice So
       Nice settings, whoever throws it - laid on the throw each browser draws, never on the message's roll, with Dice So
       Nice's ghost and secret marks kept. Daggerheart 2.10 and later colour these dice by Dice So Nice roles: nothing is
       laid there, and the diagnostic says so.
   - **What players see differently.**
     - **The roll window whole** (C5c): a player's roll window is drawn whole, as the GM's - dice, experiences,
       modifiers, formula and the mode select - with every lock kept on its section; the one-line summary and the chip
       that named the roll's audience are gone, and the mode select's tooltip says who sees the roll.
     - Their Hope and Despair dice look the table's, as above; and the player handbook says that a GM sees their dice
       fall only while that GM's Monokuma stands in their room, the result reaching the GMs either way.
   - `module.json` still reads version 1.2.97; the release commit sets the version.
   - **The package.** `git archive` lists 248 entries at 55f03746 and 249 at e8a76c53: the new `scripts/dice-look.mjs`;
     `scripts/` holds 195 module files (194 before). 53 files change (+3379, -624), one added, none removed.
   - **The stage ledger** (`tools/stages.json`, C1a and C1c): the unshipped rows in the 1.3.0 plan's order, one `planned`
     per row from 1.2.98 (35 rows change; 88 rows, 52 shipped, before and after); E22 `with` E21 (1.2.100) and E62 `with`
     E61 (1.2.109); E25 after E68 (1.2.112). E60 `planned` 1.2.98 with `touches` ["sockets", "rolls", "scenes"]; E73 moves
     from 1.2.98 to 1.2.115. No drill is named.

## Traces - one ref per trace, the band on every Remnant, D153

- 9 commits: C1a f7bb7671, C1b 5898a1a4, C1c 652c21cb, C2 d0491ae7, C4a 1834ad49, C4b 0d3fb396, and fix FG1 898e4ffc,
  FG2 c2535a2a and FG6 e8a76c53 of the fix round.
- **One read** (C1b, FG1): remnants.mjs `traceRowOf` builds a trace's row with its spot, and `traceRefsOf` the refs that
  `remnantsOn`, `remnantsInRoom`, `sceneOfRemnant` and the `...ById` helpers answer; the ten readers outside remnants.mjs
  that read a trace's token directly read its ref. Since FG1 a ref is a trace token with its row or none: a row with no
  trace token is no trace for any reader, and the GMs' store health check counts it an orphan again, as at 1.2.97 (C1b
  had made such a row a trace; the end review's correctness M1).
- **The words of D38 = 1** (C2): every comment that promised a token made at the first find, an overlay layer for traces
  or a migration says what is true; known-leaks S17-64 loses `closes: "E60"` and is held as a `foundryLimit`, with its
  README marker; 72-canary reports its check as an expected red, the known leak.

  every Remnant's band editable, found or not, the copies keeping theirs (Q-E60-1 and Q-E60-2 fell with D38 = 1); "E25

## Dice - Public roll off the panel, the dice look check, the whole roll window, one Hope and Despair look, the Monokuma rule

- 11 commits: C5a 4a375fb3, C5b 306c17ab, C5c 7bfa6fe4, C5b2 e4d06b75, C5d e984631a, C5e a9fae146, 4d05269f (R1566
  renumbered R1300: line A's numbers are R1049-R1499), 12a7a5ac (12-social's two dice checks to the owner's rule), and
  fix FG3 9bdb6995, FG4 56e90b93 and FG5 df6fbc5f; FG1, FG2 and FG6 are the traces' (above).
- **What was found** (dice/findings.md, read from the fetched sources of Dice So Nice 6.2.9 and Daggerheart 2.9.4, not
  run; the owner's screenshots the only observation): Daggerheart 2.9.4 keeps its Hope and Fear preset in a client
  setting and lays it on a die on the browser that evaluates it, so a player's and a GM's dice wore different looks (C5d);
  the small player's window was the module's own rule, E16 C2's collapse (C5c); and the GM's screen showing no player's
  dice was the GM's Dice So Nice "Show only mine" (the owner's answer of 03.11), not a code fault.
- **The dice look diagnostic** (C5b, light): scripts/dice-look.mjs, `game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook({ messageId, test })`,
  one window, its findings from a closed list of codes; the report's part *Dice look*. Since FG3 it knows the table's
  Hope and Despair look and keeps the throw history as drawn.
- **Who sees a player's dice** (C5e, FG4): private-rolls.mjs `gmsInRoomOf` and monokuma.mjs `poolOwnerOf`; the dice's
  audience, the primary's own throw of a drawn roll and Dice So Nice's decision on a GM's screen read it; the whisper and
  who reads the card are unchanged. FG4 heads a second GM's card with the roller (`quiet`), makes a Reroll's dice follow
  the *Force private player rolls* exemption, and measures the Assistant GM's own Monokuma (33-bridge-paths A17b).
- Four LIVE rows that stated who sees a player's dice now state the Monokuma rule (FG5: LIVE-E06-03, LIVE-H82-05,
  LIVE-H82-06, LIVE-E60-06), and LIVE-E33-04 names the macro.
- Tests: R1291, R1294 to R1302 (R1300 renumbered from R1566); E60-T14, E60-T15 (rewritten), E60-T16, E60-T17, E60-T18,
  E60-T21 and the mode select's tooltip test (tier 2); 12-social's dice checks (26 -> 28), 33-bridge-paths A17 and A17b,
  72-canary's bystander check with its positive control.
- **The owner's words and answers**, all 03.11.2026, after installing 1.2.97: "Usunmy funkcje public roll z gm panel";
  "Kostki, a wlasciwie ich wyglad miedzy graczami sie nie zgadzaja - cos z dice so nice sie nie zgadza. Potrzebujemy
  diagnostyki. Zrobmy to w ramach E60, skoro i tak jest male"; "Nawet gdyby rzucal statystyka, to i tak okno nie powinno
  sie zmieniac"; "Wyglad kosci jest z daggerhearta!"; on the GM's screen, "Nie powinien ich widziec, chyba ze jest w tym
  samym pokoju" and "GM ma token monokumy ktorym sie porusza". On C5: "1. lekka 2. tak 3. tak 4. tak 5. tak" - the light
  diagnostic (no bridge row, no ask of another browser), one Hope and Despair look (Q-C5-2), the player's window whole
  (Q-C5-3), a Monokuma whose GM cannot be told admits no GM (Q-C5-4), all of it in 1.2.98. "C5b - ten kafelek raczej
  powinien byc w season setup jak juz": the check in Set the season up, not on the GM panel (C5b2). "1. Jest show only
  mine - czy mam zmienic?": the cause of the GM seeing no player's dice; LIVE-E60-09 starts by switching it off.
